mechanism_narrative: A two-week recovery in WORKPLACES from -59.0 to -32.0 signals workers returning to offices, which raises weekday foot traffic and drives RETAIL_REC above its last-28-day mean over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -59.0 at t-2w to -32.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is less than or equal to its mean over the last 28 days while WORKPLACES continues to rise.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has declined monotonically from -11.6 to -22.9 over the four observed weeks, and this negative momentum will persist, pulling the next 28-day mean below the last 28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell each week from -11.6 to -22.9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC next-28-day mean is greater than last-28-day mean despite the four-week monotonic decline continuing into the forecast.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC next-28-day mean exceeds last-28-day mean while RESIDENTIAL remains above 10 for three consecutive weeks.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC next-28-day mean exceeds last-28-day mean during the January post-holiday period.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC next-28-day mean is greater than or equal to last-28-day mean while GROCERY_PHARM > 0 and RETAIL_REC < -15.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT stabilizing from -56.4 to -55.9 marks a mobility floor; when TRANSIT rises above -56 for two consecutive weeks, transit-dependent retail catch-up will lift RETAIL_REC above its last-28-day mean over four weeks.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC next-28-day mean is less than or equal to last-28-day mean while TRANSIT remains above -56 for two consecutive weeks.
